args.message:
fix(money): use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

round_money documented banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212)
but actually used ROUND_HALF_UP, so tests like round_money(2.665) ==
2.66 failed. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN to match the documented
behavior.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary

The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` implemented `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming banker's rounding.

## Change

- `src/money.py`: switch `round_money` to use `Decimal.ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, matching the documented behavior and FIN-212.

## Behavior

- `2.675` → `2.68` (half rounds to even final digit 8)
- `2.665` → `2.66` (half rounds to even final digit 6, instead of `2.67` under HALF_UP)

## CI

CI passed on this branch.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Root cause:** `src/money.py` used `Decimal.ROUND_HALF_UP`, though its docstring (and FIN-212) calls for banker's rounding, making `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` fail (e.g. `2.665` returned `2.67` instead of `2.66`).
- **Fix:** Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and changed `round_money` to quantize with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- **CI:** Ran CI on the branch (run `ci-0001`) — it passed.
- **PR:** Opened PR #101 against main, requesting review from alex: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

Per branch protection policy, I left it unmerged so a code owner can approve it.
